paper_title: Towards a More Inclusive AI Progress and Perspectives in Large Language   Model Training for the Sámi Language
caption: The distribution of tokens and sentences across different domains in the SALT dataset is shown.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of tokens (in thousands, labeled as "Tokens (K)") across eight different categories in the SALT dataset, as described in the paper "Towards a More Inclusive AI Progress and Perspectives in Large Language Model Training for the Sámi Language." The horizontal axis lists the categories in the following order: Administrative, Religion, Non-fiction, Fiction, Law, News, Science, and Blogs. The vertical axis represents the number of tokens, scaled linearly from 0 to 10,000 with major tick marks at intervals of 2,000. Each category is represented by a single light blue bar, with the exact token count labeled above each bar in dark blue text. The highest token count is observed in the "News" category, with 10,584K tokens, followed by "Administrative" with 6,472K tokens. The "Non-fiction" category contains 1,889K tokens, while "Science" has 1,626K tokens. The remaining categories have significantly fewer tokens: "Religion" (652K), "Fiction" (387K), "Law" (354K), and "Blogs" (32K). The bars are arranged in the order of their categories along the x-axis, and no grouping or stacking is present. The chart visually emphasizes the dominance of the "News" and "Administrative" categories in terms of token volume, with "Blogs" being the smallest by a large margin.
